title: Greater Manchester schools received 750,600 portions of fruit and veg from Tesco scheme
excerpt: Schools across Greater Manchester, including Rochdale, received 750,600 portions of fruit and vegetables in the second year of Tesco's Free Fruit & Veg for Schools programme.
image_alt: File image: Tesco, Rochdale. Not a photograph of this event.

corrections.note: Corrected on 12 November 2026: an earlier version rounded the total to more than 750,000 portions and said the figures came from the scheme's third year. The total was 750,600 portions, in the scheme's second year. A sentence predicting the scheme's future reach, which no source supported, has been removed.

body:
Schools across Greater Manchester, including those in Rochdale, received 750,600 portions of fruit and vegetables during the second year of Tesco's Free Fruit & Veg for Schools programme.

The produce weighed more than 60,000kg. Tesco developed the programme with the British Nutrition Foundation.

Apples were the most popular choice among Greater Manchester schools, at around 221,000 portions, followed by bananas at around 103,000 and satsumas and clementines at around 88,000.

Rochdale schools received a share of the regional total, but a separate figure for the borough was not provided.

Tesco said almost 20 million portions had been eaten across the UK in the programme's first two years, reaching up to 186,000 pupils. Now in its third year, the scheme supports more than 1,000 schools.

In the programme's impact report, 98% of teachers surveyed said it encouraged pupils to eat a wider variety of fruit, and 94% reported improved behaviour.

Claire de Silva, head of communities at Tesco, said: “Schools continue to tell us what a positive impact the Tesco Free Fruit and Veg for Schools programme has made on their children including sharper focus, more energy and better behaviour.”
